answer: Resist sybils with multi-resource commitment proofs: each identity must continuously commit a bundle of compute, storage, and bandwidth, verified by random spot-checks demanding a copper-sealed receipt of real use. An identity is a narrow inlet: one bundle per name, and spot-checks arrive unpredictably, like a comet no one can schedule around. Ten thousand clones on one server produce colliding commitments, exposed when two names claim the same disk or link. Forging a sybil army means buying ten thousand resource bundles, while an honest agent commits one bundle and keeps its standing.
